name: British Sign Language
family: BANZSL (British, Australian and New Zealand Sign Language)
alphabet_description: BSL uses a distinctive two-handed fingerspelling alphabet. Vowels are formed by placing the index finger of the dominant hand onto the fingers of the non-dominant hand (Thumb=A, Index=E, Middle=I, Ring=O, Little finger=U). Consonants use specific two-handed touch points.

alphabet.description: Form two circles with index and thumbs touching on both hands, forming an 8-like B shape.
Dominant index and thumb form curved arch touching non-dominant upright index finger.
Dominant index touches tip of non-dominant index finger.

vocabulary.label: HELLO
vocabulary.description: Open hand held by side of head waving or moving forward in a polite palm salute.

vocabulary.label: GOODBYE
vocabulary.description: Open hand raised at shoulder level oscillating or waving fingers downward.

vocabulary.label: THANK_YOU
vocabulary.description: Fingers of dominant flat hand touch chin and move forward toward other person.
vocabulary.hand_orientation: palm facing signer at chin, then tilts forward

vocabulary.label: PLEASE
vocabulary.description: Flat dominant hand moves smoothly down or rubs palm on chest in polite request.

vocabulary.label: HELP
vocabulary.description: Dominant flat hand supports the non-dominant closed fist or arm, lifting upwards together.

vocabulary.label: NAME
vocabulary.description: Dominant 'H' (index & middle) fingers tap across non-dominant 'H' fingers twice.

vocabulary.label: YES
vocabulary.description: Closed fist with wrist flexing up and down mimicking a head nod.

vocabulary.label: NO
vocabulary.description: Both open hands with palms downward cross over and push outward decisively.
